//: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the ecosystem's pinned vendor versions: the framework/native/styling stack, plus EVERY native module compiled into the EAS binary even when only one feature uses it (e.g. @shopify/flash-list, the react-native-drax fork). scripts/write-workspace-root.ts transcribes these into the workspace root's pnpm `overrides:` block and package-versions.json; the Go OTA rebuild (core/server/pkgbuild) re-renders the same block from the root copy. Bump in lockstep with each native (EAS) build. Feature-specific pure-JS libraries do NOT belong here — a feature declares those itself. The metro, metro-cache and metro-transform-worker pins equal the exact metro version @expo/metro pins for this SDK: uniwind declares them as unversioned peers, and without the pin pnpm resolves them to the newest metro, so uniwind would patch a metro copy Expo never runs. @react-native/metro-config and @types/react follow react-native and react for the same single-copy reason. A SECOND class of entry also lives here: advisory-driven floors on transitive dependencies (e.g. postcss, js-yaml) pulled in deep under expo/@expo/cli/metro/react-native-community-cli. No feature or member declares these directly, so a feature cannot 'declare it itself' — the overrides block is the only place that can express a floor on a package nothing in the tree depends on by name. These are bumped when a security advisory requires it, not in lockstep with a native build; do not read them as EAS-binary pins.
